what: Dow makes basic chemicals and plastics: polyethylene for packaging, silicones for construction and electronics, and industrial intermediates used in paints, coatings and insulation.
customers: Packaging converters, construction and infrastructure companies, car and electronics manufacturers, and consumer goods makers.
money: polyurethanes, industrial solutions and construction chemicals
moat: World-scale plants on the US Gulf Coast using cheap American natural gas liquids as feedstock, which gives a cost advantage over naphtha-based European and Asian producers.
risks: It reported a loss as chemical prices fell to cycle lows
Revenue has fallen about 11% a year over three years
It cut its dividend to preserve cash
opportunities: A dividend yield around 4.5% even after the cut
Analysts see about 16% upside from current levels
Low-cost US feedstock means it is among the last producers to lose money in a downturn
watch: Polyethylene spreads and whether chemical prices have bottomed.
